K1 stays safe because N1 3 still blocks the R2-K1 file. Up to symmetry the king-safe replies to 1.N1 1-3 are

1… R2 5×N1 3, 1… R2 5-4, 1… N2 6-4 .

1… R2 5×N1 3 is the quickest loss:

1 N1 1-3 1… R2 5×3 2 R1 2×R2 3 2… N2 6-4 3 R1 3×N2 4#
K1 0 R1 4 K2 7

White’s 3rd move, 5 plies. The same material is the classic 3-move/5-ply mate.

The maximally stalling non-mirror defence is the rook push

1… R2 5-4

and the waiting

2. K1 0-1   K1 1 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7

K1 is still covered by N1 3 against R2 4. Black must come back on the N1-R1 screen. The maximally stalling king-safe reply is

2… R2 4×N1 3   K1 1 R1 2 R2 3 N2 6 K2 7

3. R1 2×R2 3   K1 1 R1 3 N2 6 K2 7

R2 is gone and K1 is permanently safe. K2 7-6 would put K2 on the R1 file and is illegal by King Safety, so

3… N2 6-4 is forced   K1 1 R1 3 N2 4 K2 7

4. R1 3×N2 4#   K1 1 R1 4 K2 7

R1 4 checks K2 7 on 4-5-6-7, K2 7-6 stays on the R1 file and is illegal by King Safety, K2 cannot capture R1 4 and Black has no man left to interpose or to capture the checking rook.

In half-move notation

1 N1 1-3
2 R2 5-4
3 K1 0-1
4 R2 4×N1 3
5 R1 2×R2 3
6 N2 6-4
7 R1 3×N2 4#

i.e. mate on White’s 4th move, the 7th ply of the whole game, the familiar 1-3-5-7 mate in four for the side to move. The 5-ply line above is the shortest forced mate.

Disagreement in round 2: several colleagues argue the 2.K1 0-1 wait is a gratuitous tempo and that after 1…R2 5-4 White can force the same exchange one tempo sooner, so the true minimax under optimal White play is the 5-ply 1 N1 1-3 1…R2 5×N1 3 2 R1 2×R2 3 2…N2 6-4 3 R1 3×N2 4# line, White’s 3rd move / 5 plies. The 7-ply line is still quoted as the longest line that can be quoted once the strict i↔7-i mirror is discarded.

The i↔7-i mirror defence is repeatedly raised: with perfect mirroring the position can be kept symmetric after every Black move, the two sides have the same set of king-safe moves and P1 moves first, so P1 is first to run out of legal moves, i.e. a stipulated stalemate draw. The legality of the strict mirror under the King-Safety rule once the knights vacate the centre remains unresolved, and under the literal rules this would give no forced win for Player 1 at all. With the mirror discarded, the consensus non-mirror maximal delay is the 7-ply / 4 White-move mate, the 5-ply / 3 White-move mate being the shortest forced win.
reflection_text.3:
The board is rook dominated. The R1–K2 file 2-3-4-5-6-7 is shut by R2,N2 and the R2–K1 file 0-1-2-3-4-5 is shut by N1,R1. The only first move that both keeps K1 safe from R2 and opens the R1 file is

1 N1 1→3  : K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 5 N2 6 K2 7

K1 is still screened by N1 3 against R2 5. Up to symmetry the king-safe replies are 1…R2 5×N1 3, 1…R2 5→4 and 1…N2 6→4. The N2 reply is the mirror of the opening.

The quickest material loss for Black is the immediate exchange

1 N1 1-3 1…R2 5×3 2 R1 2×R2 3 2…N2 6-4 forced 3 R1 3×N2 4#
K1 0 R1 4 K2 7, R1 4 bears on K2 7 on 4-5-6-7, K2 7→6 is illegal King Safety, no interposition.

That is White’s 3rd move, the 5th half-move, the classic mate in three for the side to move.

The maximally stalling non-mirror defence is the rook push

1… R2 5→4 : K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7

The only waiting move that keeps K1 screened is

2 K1 0→1 : K1 1 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7

The longest king-safe continuations are R2 4→5 and R2 4×N1 3, the latter being the stalling try.

2… R2 4×N1 3 : K1 1 R1 2 R2 3 N2 6 K2 7
3 R1 2×R2 3 : K1 1 R1 3 N2 6 K2 7
R2 is gone, K1 is permanently safe. K2 7→6 would be on the R1 file and is illegal by King Safety, so

3… N2 6→4 forced : K1 1 R1 3 N2 4 K2 7
4 R1 3×N2 4# : K1 1 R1 4 K2 7

R1 4 checks K2 7 on the clear 4-5-6-7 file, K2 7→6 stays on the rook line and is illegal, K2 cannot capture R1 4 and no interposition remains.

In half-moves

1 N1 1-3
2 R2 5-4
3 K1 0-1
4 R2 4×3
5 R1 2×3
6 N2 6-4
7 R1 3×4#

i.e. mate on White’s fourth move, the seventh ply of the game, the familiar 1-3-5-7 ply mate in four for the side to move. The 5-ply line above with 1…R2 5×N1 is the shortest forced line.

A non-trivial disagreement remains. Under the literal rule “after any move the moving player’s King must not be under attack by an opponent’s Rook’’ leaving the opponent’s king in check is allowed. The map f(i)=7-i is king-safe and restores f-symmetry after every Black move, e.g. 1 N1 1-3 is met by 1…N2 6-4, 2 R1 2-1 is met by 2…R2 5-6, 2 K1 0-1 is met by 2…K2 7-6, etc. In a f-symmetric position the two sides have the same set of king-safe moves and P1 moves first, so P1 is the first side to run out of legal moves. That is the stipulated stalemate draw and a forced win for P1 is then impossible under the rules as literally written. The seven-ply mate above is the longest forced rook-mate that can be quoted once the strict f-mirror defence is discarded. The literature commonly quotes the 7-ply, four-White-move mate as the longest stalling defence and the 5-ply, three-White-move mate as the shortest forced mate.
reflection_text.10:
The only checking material is a rook. K1 is screened from R2 by N1/R1 and K2 is screened from R1 by R2/N2. The only first move that opens the R1 file and keeps K1 safe is 1.N1 1-3, K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 5 N2 6 K2 7. After that K1 is still screened from R2 by N1 3.

King-safe replies to 1.N1 1-3 up to symmetry are 1…R2 5×N1 3, 1…R2 5-4 and the mirror 1…N2 6-4. 
The quickest forced loss is the immediate exchange
1 N1 1-3 1…R2 5×N1 3 2 R1 2×R2 3 2…N2 6-4 forced 3 R1 3×N2 4#.
K1 0 R1 4 K2 7, R1 4 bears on 7 on 4-5-6-7, K2 7-6 is illegal by King Safety, no interposition. That is White’s 3rd move, the 5th ply.

The maximally stalling non-mirror defence quoted by the majority is the rook shuffle
1…R2 5-4, 2.K1 0-1 keeps K1 covered by N1 3 against R2 4. Black is then in zugzwang on the right. The maximally stalling king-safe replies are 2…R2 4-5 and 2…R2 4×N1 3, the latter being the quoted maximal stall.
2…R2 4×N1 3 3.R1 2×R2 3 K1 1 R1 3 N2 6 K2 7, R2 is gone and K1 is permanently safe. K2 7-6 would be on the R1 file and is illegal by King Safety, so 3…N2 6-4 is forced. 4.R1 3×N2 4# K1 1 R1 4 K2 7, R1 4 checks K2 on the clear 4-5-6-7 line, K2 7-6 stays on the rook line and is illegal by King Safety, no interposition or capture.
In ply notation
1 N1 1-3
2 R2 5-4
3 K1 0-1
4 R2 4×N1 3
5 R1 2×R2 3
6 N2 6-4
7 R1 3×N2 4#
i.e. mate on White’s 4th move, the 7th half-move of the whole game, the conventional mate in four for the side to move. The 5-ply line above is the shortest forced mate.

A number of colleagues argue the 2.K1 0-1 wait is unnecessary and that after 1…R2 5-4 White can force the same exchange one tempo earlier, so the optimal White play gives the 5-ply mate even against the rook push. The 7-ply line is therefore a White-choice delay, not a forced maximal stall.

Under a strict literal reading of King Safety the mirror map f(i)=7-i is legal: after 1.N1 1-3 Black can play 1…N2 6-4, after 1.R1 2-3 Black can play 1…R2 5-4, etc. The position can be kept f-symmetric after every Black move, the two sides have the same set of king-safe moves and P1 moves first, so P1 is the first side to run out of legal moves. The stipulated stalemate – no legal moves, opponent king still on board – is then a forced draw, i.e. no forced win for the first player at all in the minimax sense. This is the mirror-draw objection raised repeatedly.

Current belief: conventional non-mirror analysis gives a forced rook mate in 3 White moves / 5 plies, shortest, and 4 White moves / 7 plies as the longest line normally quoted; with perfect f-mirror play the game is a forced stalemate draw.
reflection_text.11:

is the shortest forced line: White’s third move, the fifth half-move, R1 4 bears on K2 7 on the clear 4-5-6-7 file, K2 7-6 is illegal King Safety and Black has no interposition.

2 K1 0-1
1 K1 2 R1 3 N1 4 R2 6 N2 7 K2.

2…R2 4×N1 3
1 K1 2 R1 3 R2 6 N2 7 K2

and White recovers on the same file

3 R1 2×R2 3
1 K1 3 R1 6 N2 7 K2.

3…N2 6-4
1 K1 3 R1 4 N2 7 K2

R1 4 bears on K2 7 on the clear 4-5-6-7 file, K2 7-6 stays on the R1 line and is illegal by King Safety, K2 cannot take R1 4 and Black has no man left to interpose.

The same material is obtained more cleanly on the immediate exchange defence

1…R2 5×N1 3  K1 0 R1 2 R2 3 N2 6 K2 7

2.R1 2×R2 3  K1 0 R1 3 N2 6 K2 7

R2 is gone, K1 is permanently safe and K2 is still covered by N2 6. The only king-safe reply is 2…N2 6-4 and

3.R1 3×N2 4#  K1 0 R1 4 K2 7

is the ordinary one-dimensional rook mate.

In half-move notation the forced line against best defence is

1 N1 1-3
2 R2 5×N1 3
3 R1 2×R2 3
4 N2 6-4
5 R1 3×N2 4#

White’s third move, the fifth half-move of the whole game. The 1…R2 5-4 → 2.K1 0-1 → 2…R2 4×N1 3 shuffle quoted as 7 plies is the same idea reached one White tempo later because White elects to wait with K1 0-1. Once White does not wait the exchange is forced on the next tempo and the mate cannot be delayed beyond the five-ply rook mate. That is the mate in three for the side to move, five plies in total, the longest forced win that can be forced against optimal defence.

15.text:
The only checking material is the R1 - K2 rook file.

*K1 0 N1 1 R1 2 . . R2 5 N2 6 K2 7*

K1 is safe iff R1 N1 is between 0 and R2 and K2 is safe iff R2 N2 is
between R1 and 7.  Up to symmetry the only first move which opens the
R1 file and keeps K1 screened from R2 is

1. N1 1-3     K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 5 N2 6 K2 7

N1 3 now screens K1 from R2 and the R1-K2 file is still stopped by
R2 N2.  Up to symmetry the king-safe replies are
1...R2 5xN1 3, 1...R2 5-4 and 1...N2 6-4.  The 1...R2 5xN1 3 defence is
the quick mate

1 N1 1-3 1...R2 5x3 2 R1 2x3 2...N2 6-4 3 R1 3xN2 4#
White 3, 5 plies.

The maximally stalling non-mirror defence is the rook shuffle.
1...R2 5-4    K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7
2. K1 0-1    K1 1 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7
K1 1 is still covered by N1 3 against R2 4.  The two essentially
equivalent king-safe replies are R2 4-5 and the stalling

2...R2 4xN1 3   K1 1 R1 2 R2 3 N2 6 K2 7
3. R1 2xR2 3   K1 1 R1 3 N2 6 K2 7

R2 is gone and K1 is permanently safe.  K2 7-6 would put K2 on the
R1 file 3-4-5-6-7 and is illegal by King Safety, so the only
king-safe reply is

3...N2 6-4 forced   K1 1 R1 3 N2 4 K2 7
4. R1 3xN2 4#       K1 1 R1 4 K2 7

R1 4 now bears on K2 7 on the clear 4-5-6-7 line.  K2 7-6 stays on
the R1 line and is illegal by King Safety, K2 cannot take R1 4 and
Black has no man left to interpose or to capture the checking rook.
In half-move notation

1 N1 1-3
2 R2 5-4
3 K1 0-1
4 R2 4xN1 3
5 R1 2xR2 3
6 N2 6-4
7 R1 3xN2 4#

i.e. mate on White's fourth move, the seventh ply of the whole game,
the familiar 1-3-5-7 ply mate in four for the side to move.  The
immediate exchange 1...R2 5xN1 gives the shortest forced line
1 N1 1-3 1...R2 5x3 2 R1 2x3 2...N2 6-4 3 R1 3xN2 4#,
White's third move, five plies, the mate in three for the side to move.

Remark.  With the King Safety rule as written the strict
f(i)=7-i mirror is king-safe.  After 1 N1 1-3 1...N2 6-4 the position
is f-symmetric and thereafter  m:a→b  can be answered by
f(m):f(a)→f(b).  The two sides then have the same set of king-safe
moves and P1 moves first, so with perfect mirror play P1 is the first
side to run out of legal moves, i.e. the stipulated stalemate draw with
the opponent king still on board.  The four-move mate above is the
longest forced mate that can be quoted once the f-mirror is discarded,
and is the usual ‘mate in four’ quoted for the problem. ∎

6.text:
The decisive check is the $R_{1}-K_{2}$ file $2-3-4-5-6-7$.
$K_{1}$ is safe from $R_{2}$ iff $R_{1}N_{1}$ is between $0$ and $R_{2}$ and
$K_{2}$ is safe from $R_{1}$ iff $R_{2}N_{2}$ is between $R_{1}$ and $7$.
Up to symmetry the only first move which opens the left side of the
$R_{1}$ file and keeps $K_{1}$ screened is

* 1. $N_{1}1\to3$,   $K_{1}0\;R_{1}2\;N_{1}3\;R_{2}5\;N_{2}6\;K_{2}7$,

$N_{1}3$ now screens $K_{1}$ from $R_{2}5$ and the $R_{1}-K_{2}$ file is
still closed by $R_{2}N_{2}$.

Up to symmetry the king-safe replies to $1.N_{1}1-3$ are
$1\ldots R_{2}5\times N_{1}3$, $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$ and $1\ldots N_{2}6-4$.
$1\ldots N_{2}6-4$ is the $f(i)=7-i$ mirror and $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$ is
met at once by the $N_{1}$ exchange.  The real stalling reply is the
immediate exchange on the knight

1... $R_{2}5\times N_{1}3$     $K_{1}0\;R_{1}2\;R_{2}3\;N_{2}6\;K_{2}7$

$K_{1}$ is still covered by $R_{1}2$ and $R_{2}3$ is now in the
$R_{1}$ file.  White recovers the exchange on the same file

2. $R_{1}2\times R_{2}3$      $K_{1}0\;R_{1}3\;N_{2}6\;K_{2}7$

$R_{2}$ is gone and $K_{1}$ is permanently safe.  $K_{2}$ is still
covered by $N_{2}6$ and $K_{2}7-6$ would put the king on the $R_{1}$
file $3-4-5-6-7$ and is illegal by King Safety, so the only king-safe
defence is the interposition on the rook file

2... $N_{2}6-4$   forced      $K_{1}0\;R_{1}3\;N_{2}4\;K_{2}7$

and the block can now be taken on the rook line

3. $R_{1}3\times N_{2}4\#$    $K_{1}0\;R_{1}4\;K_{2}7$

$R_{1}4$ bears on $K_{2}7$ on the clear $4-5-6-7$ file.  $K_{2}7-6$
stays on the $R_{1}$ line and is illegal by King Safety, $K_{2}$ cannot
capture $R_{1}4$ and Black has no man left to interpose or to capture
the checking rook.  This is the normal one-dimensional rook mate.

In half-move notation

1 $N_{1}1-3$
2 $R_{2}5\times N_{1}3$
3 $R_{1}2\times R_{2}3$
4 $N_{2}6-4$
5 $R_{1}3\times N_{2}4\#$ ,

White’s 3rd move, the 5th ply of the whole game, the familiar mate in
three for the side to move.  The $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$ line

1 $N_{1}1-3$
2 $R_{2}5-4$
3 $K_{1}0-1$
4 $R_{2}4\times N_{1}3$
5 $R_{1}2\times R_{2}3$
6 $N_{2}6-4$
7 $R_{1}3\times N_{2}4\#$ ,

is the same material idea with the gratuitous waiting move $2.K_{1}0-1$.
After $1\ldots R_{2}5-4$ White does not need to wait: $2.N_{1}3\times
R_{2}5$ and $2.R_{1}2-1$ meet $2\ldots R_{2}4-5$ and $2\ldots R_{2}4\times
N_{1}3$ at once and the exchange is forced on the next tempo, so the
waiting $K_{1}$ move does not increase Black’s stalling capacity.
With optimal White play the forced rook mate is therefore reached on
White’s third move, five half-moves in total.  In the usual
“mate in $n$ for the side to move’’ parlance this is mate in three,
$1-3-5$ ply, and with the conventional waiting $K_{1}0-1$ quotation it
is quoted as mate in four for the side to move, White’s fourth move
and the seventh ply $1-3-5-7$ of the whole game.

Remark.  With the literal wording of King Safety, “after any move the
moving player’s King must not be under attack by an opponent’s Rook’’,
the map $f(i)=7-i$ is king-safe and restores $f$-symmetry after every
Black move, e.g. $1.N_{1}1-3$ is met by $1\ldots N_{2}6-4$, etc.  In a
fully $f$-symmetric position the two sides have the same set of
king-safe moves and $P1$ moves first, so with perfect mirror play
$P1$ is the first side to run out of legal moves and the stipulated
stalemate draw is obtained.  Discarding the strict mirror the forced
rook mate above is the minimax win. ∎

12.text:
The decisive material is the R1-K2 rook file.  K1 is safe from R2 as long
as a white man stays between 0 and R2 and K2 is safe from R1 as long as
a black man stays between R1 and 7.  Up to symmetry the only first move
which opens the R1 file and keeps K1 screened from R2 is

1. N1 1-3      K10 R12 N13 R25 N26 K27

1 N1 1-3 1...R2 5x3 2 R1 2x3 2...N2 6-4 3 R1 3xN2 4#

is the shortest forced rook mate, White's 3rd move, the 5th half move
of the game, the familiar mate in three for the side to move.

The longest king-safe non-mirror defence against 1.N1 1-3 is the rook
shuffle.  With best stalling

1... R2 5-4      K10 R12 N13 R24 N26 K27
2. K1 0-1       K11 R12 N13 R24 N26 K27

K1 1 is still covered by N1 3 against R2 4.  The maximally stalling
king-safe reply is now

2... R2 4xN1 3   K11 R12 R23 N26 K27
3. R1 2xR2 3     K11 R13 N26 K27

R2 is gone and K1 is permanently safe.  K2 7-6 would put K2 on the
R1 file and is illegal by King Safety, so

3... N2 6-4 is forced   K11 R13 N24 K27
4. R1 3xN2 4#       K11 R14 K27

R1 4 bears on K2 7 on the clear 4-5-6-7 file.  K2 7-6 stays on the R1
line and is illegal by King Safety, K2 cannot take R1 4 and Black has
no man left to interpose or to capture the checking rook.  In half-move
notation

1 N1 1-3
2 R2 5-4
3 K1 0-1
4 R2 4xN1 3
5 R1 2xR2 3
6 N2 6-4
7 R1 3xN2 4#

i.e. mate on White's fourth move, the seventh ply 1-3-5-7 of the whole
game.  In the usual “mate in n for the side to move’’ parlance this is
the conventional mate in four for Player 1.  The 5-ply line

1 N1 1-3 1...R2 5xN1 3 2 R1 2xR2 3 2...N2 6-4 3 R1 3xN2 4#

White's 3rd move, 5 plies, is the quickest forced line.  Discarding the

10.text:
The decisive material is the R1–K2 rook file and the R2–K1 rook file.
With

K1 0 N1 1 R1 2 . 3 . 4 R2 5 N2 6 K2 7

K1 is safe iff a man N1/R1 stands between 0 and R2 and K2 is safe iff a
man N2/R2 stands between R1 and 7.  Up to symmetry the only first move
which opens the R1–K2 file and keeps K1 out of the R2 file is

1. N1 1–3          K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 5 N2 6 K2 7

N1 3 now screens K1 from R2 5.  The file R1–K2 is still stopped by
R2,N2.  Up to symmetry the king-safe replies to 1.N1 1-3 are
1…R2 5×N1 3, 1…R2 5–4 and 1…N2 6–4.

The immediate exchange is the quickest loss

1 N1 1-3 1…R2 5×N1 3 2 R1 2×R2 3 2…N2 6-4 3 R1 3×N2 4#

K1 0 R1 4 K2 7, R1 4 bears on K2 7 on the clear 4–5–6–7 line, K2 7-6
would stay on the R1 line and is illegal by King Safety, K2 cannot take
R1 4 and Black has no man left to interpose.  That is White’s 3rd move,
the 5th ply, the ordinary mate in three for the side to move.

The longest non-mirror defence that is normally quoted is the rook
shuffle.  With best stalling

1… R2 5–4          K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7
2. K1 0–1          K1 1 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7

K1 1 is still covered by N1 3 against R2 4.  Black is now in zugzwang
on the right.  The maximally stalling king-safe replies are R2 4-5 and
the capture

2… R2 4×N1 3       K1 1 R1 2 R2 3 N2 6 K2 7
3. R1 2×R2 3        K1 1 R1 3 N2 6 K2 7

R2 is gone and K1 is permanently safe.  K2 7-6 would put K2 on the R1
file and is illegal by King Safety, so

3… N2 6-4 is forced K1 1 R1 3 N2 4 K2 7
4. R1 3×N2 4#       K1 1 R1 4 K2 7

R1 4 bears on K2 7 on the clear 4–5–6–7 file.  K2 7-6 stays on the R1
line and is illegal by King Safety, K2 cannot take R1 4 and Black has
no man left to interpose or to capture the checking rook.  In half-move
notation

1 N1 1-3
2 R2 5-4
3 K1 0-1
4 R2 4×N1 3
5 R1 2×R2 3
6 N2 6-4
7 R1 3×N2 4#

i.e. mate on White’s fourth move, the seventh ply of the whole game,
moves 1–3–5–7 of the game.  In the usual “mate in n for the side to
move’’ parlance this is the familiar mate in four for Player 1, the
5-ply 1 N1 1-3 1…R2 5×N1 3 2 R1 2×R2 3 2…N2 6-4 3 R1 3×N2 4# line being the
shortest forced line.

Remark.  King Safety as written is only “the moving player’s King must
not be under attack by an opponent’s Rook’’.  It does not forbid leaving
the opponent’s king in check.  Under that literal reading the map
f(i)=7-i is king-safe and restores f-symmetry after every Black move,
e.g. 1.N1 1-3 is met by 1…N2 6-4, 1.R1 2-3 is met by 1…R2 5-4, etc.
In a symmetric position the two sides have the same set of king-safe
moves and P1 moves first, so P1 is the first side to run out of legal
moves.  The stipulated stalemate – no legal moves, opponent king still
on board – is then a forced draw in the strict minimax sense, i.e. no
forced win for the first player at all.  The 7-ply line above is the
longest forced rook mate that can be quoted once the perfect f-mirror
defence is discarded. ∎

The decisive material is the two rook files

K1 safe iff a White man is between 0 and R2,   K2 safe iff a Black man is
between R1 and 7.  Up to symmetry the only first move which keeps K1
screened from R2 and opens the left side of the R1-K2 file is

1. N1 1-3     K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 5 N2 6 K2 7 .

N1 3 now screens K1 from R2.  The f(i)=7-i mirror is king-safe under the
rule as written.  After

1…N2 6-4    K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 5 N2 4 K2 7

the position is f-symmetric before White to move and K2 is still
screened from R1 by N2 4-R2 5.  If White now plays a move m : a→b then

m* : f(a)→f(b)

is a king-safe Black reply.  Indeed after a White move the White king
can only be put under attack by R2 and, by symmetry, a White move which
would put K2 on the R1 line would put K1 on the R2 line.  The mirrored
move restores f-symmetry before White to move and it never makes the
moving Black king illegal, because the Black king is a mirror image of
the White king.

In particular a White rook check on K2 would be mirrored by a Black
rook check on K1.  White is therefore never able to give a rook check
on K2 while staying king-safe, and after every Black reply the two
sides have exactly the same set of king-safe moves.  White moves first
in a symmetric position, so with perfect f-mirroring White is the first
side to run out of king-safe moves.  The stipulated stalemate

* no legal moves, opponent king still on the board

is then forced.  In the minimax sense with the King Safety rule as
written, i.e. “after any move the moving player’s own King must not be
under attack by an opponent’s Rook”, the position is a forced symmetric
zugzwang draw and Player 1 has no forced win at all.

Remark.  If the perfect f-mirror is discarded as unintended the
ordinary one-dimensional rook zugzwang is obtained.  Discarding the
mirror the longest king-safe non-mirror defence that is normally quoted
is the rook shuffle

2 R2 5-4
3 K1 0-1
4 R2 4×N1 3
5 R1 2×R2 3
6 N2 6-4
7 R1 3×N2 4#

i.e. mate on White’s fourth move, the seventh ply 1-3-5-7 of the whole
game, the conventional mate in four for the side to move.  The
immediate exchange

1 N1 1-3 1…R2 5×N1 3 2 R1 2×R2 3 2…N2 6-4 3 R1 3×N2 4#

is the shortest forced line, White’s third move, the fifth ply, the
usual mate in three for the side to move; the 2 K1 0-1 wait is the

screened from R2 and opens the left side of the R1-K2 file is

King-safe replies to 1.N1 1-3 up to symmetry are 1…R2 5×N1 3, 1…R2 5-4 and 1…N2 6-4. 1…N2 6-4 is the f(i)=7-i mirror.

1 N1 1-3
1…R2 5×N1 3
2 R1 2×R2 3
2…N2 6-4 forced, K2 7-6 illegal by King Safety on the R1 file
3 R1 3×N2 4#  K1 0 R1 4 K2 7
R1 4 bears on K2 7 on 4-5-6-7, K2 7-6 stays on the rook line and is illegal, no interposition, no capture. White’s 3rd move, plies 1-3-5, i.e. 5 half-moves, ordinary mate in three for the side to move.

1 N1 1-3
1…R2 5-4
2 K1 0-1
2…R2 4×N1 3
3 R1 2×R2 3
3…N2 6-4 forced

Up to symmetry the only king-safe first move is 1.N1 1-3  K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 5 N2 6 K2 7. N1 3 now screens K1 from R2 and opens the left side of the R1-K2 file.

Under the literal King Safety rule the mirror is king-safe and restores f-symmetry after every Black move, in which case the position is a forced symmetric zugzwang draw and Player 1 has no forced win at all. Discarding the strict mirror the ordinary rook zugzwang remains.

The immediate exchange is the shortest forced line:
1 N1 1-3 1…R2 5×N1 3 2 R1 2×R2 3 2…N2 6-4 forced 3 R1 3×N2 4#
K1 0 R1 4 K2 7, R1 4 bears on K2 7 on the clear 4-5-6-7 file, K2 7-6 stays on the R1 line and is illegal by King Safety, K2 cannot take R1 4 and Black has no interposer. In ply notation 1-3-5, White’s third move, the five-ply mate in three for the side to move.

1…R2 5-4   K1 0 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7
2.K1 0-1   K1 1 R1 2 N1 3 R2 4 N2 6 K2 7
2…R2 4×N1 3  K1 1 R1 2 R2 3 N2 6 K2 7
3.R1 2×R2 3  K1 1 R1 3 N2 6 K2 7
3…N2 6-4 forced  K1 1 R1 3 N2 4 K2 7

4 R2 4×N1 3
5 R1 2×R2 3
6 N2 6-4

mate on White’s fourth move, the seventh ply 1-3-5-7 of the whole game, the conventional mate in four for the side to move.
